newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem says government will honor pensions ruling.
newsitem.headline: Menem says government will honor pensions ruling.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem said Sunday the government will honor Friday's ruling by the Supreme Court on increases in backdated pension payments.
"Something is certain, and that is the payment of this obligation because this is about a Supreme Court ruling," President Menem said at a press conference, according to state news agency Telam.
Argentina's Supreme Court ruled Friday on a case brought by 70,000 pensioners that state pension payments from 1991 to 1994 will be adjusted upwards by 13.8 percent.

The ruling reestablished the mobility of pension payments in line with increases in the cost of living. The government's convertibility plan introduced in 1991, pegging the value of the peso to the dollar at par, fixed pension payments.

It was still unclear how large or by when the government will have to make the payments, although Guillermo Lopez, one of the ministers of the Supreme Court said Saturday the full bill will be $4.0 billion, according to local media.
Still, Menem said "as this ruling comes after next year's budget is completed we will not be able to include this payment."

The president added that there is a fund of 20 million pesos "which we will begin to use to pay and honor our debt to the pensioners." He added that there are some $200 million worth of bonds that the government intends to use as payment as well.
Menem emphasised that this ruling would in no way threaten convertibility.
